published_statement: p.10: 'The massive Klein-Gordon field in 4-dimensional Minkowski space obeys the following bound [22] INT <T00>_w(t,x)|g(t)|^2 dt >= -(1/16pi^3) INT_m^oo |g^(u)|^2 u^4 Q3(u/m) du (1) for any smooth compactly supported g, and all Hadamard states w ... In the m = 0 case, the bound simplifies, and actually gives a bound valid for all m >= 0: INT <T00>_w(t,x) g(t)^2 dt >= -(1/16pi^2) INT |g''(t)|^2 dt. (3)' Notes: 'The left-hand side depends on the quantum state w, while the right-hand side is state-independent. The bound is known not to be optimal. The bound requires a certain degree of smoothness in g ... remains valid if one take g to be an element of the Sobolev space W^{2,2}(R) ... does not apply to g with lower regularity ... By sharp switching, one can trap arbitrarily large negative energy densities.' p.11: 'Suppose that <T00>_w < rho for some interval t in [t0, t0+tau] of time. Then, for any g in C0^oo((t0,t0+tau)) ... <g|g''''>/<g|g> >= -16pi^2 rho ... the left-hand side can be minimized over g, to give the minimum eigenvalue of the operator d^4/dt^4 on [t0,t0+tau], with boundary conditions at each end corresponding to vanishing of the function and its first derivative. The upshot is that rho >= -C/tau^4, (4) where the numerical constant C ~ 3.17. Turning this around, in any time interval of duration tau, the energy density must at some instant exceed -C/tau^4. Tighter results may be obtained for massive fields [16].' p.13: 'Consider a region between Casimir plates at z = +-L/2 in otherwise flat spacetime and an inertial trajectory parallel to the plates. Let l be the distance from this trajectory to the nearest plate in the t = 0 surface. Then no experiment conducted along the trajectory in a time interval of less than 2l can possibly know about the existence of the plates; it should be as if the experiment was conducted in Minkowski space. In particular the quantum energy inequalities apply, and [as the energy density is supposed constant along the trajectory] (4) gives an a priori bound T00 >= -C/(2l)^4 ~ -3.17/(2l)^4 = -0.20/l^4. By comparison, the known value of the Casimir energy density for the massless minimally coupled scalar field is T00 = -pi^2/(1140 L^4) - (pi^2/(48 L^4))(3 - 2cos^2(pi z/L))/cos^4(pi z/L) which ranges between 3-7% of the bound as z varies in [-L/2, L/2].' p.14: 'the a priori bound ... also applies to all stationary (Hadamard) states of the system ... There remains an interesting question as to why the Casimir energy density is a comparatively small proportion of the allowed bound.' 2301.01698 p.2: massless field, inertial worldline, Minkowski vacuum reference, 'Using the evenness of |g^|^2 together with Parseval's theorem then yields INT ds |g(s)|^2 <:T_mn u^m u^n:>_w >= -(1/16pi^2) INT |g''(s)|^2 ds (1.4)', valid 'for all real-valued compactly supported smooth test functions g, and all Hadamard states'.
published_hypotheses: P1 free real scalar (Klein-Gordon) field, MINIMAL coupling (Sec. 2.5 'energy density (of the minimally coupled field)'); Eq.(3) valid for all mass m >= 0
P3 averaging along an INERTIAL worldline (Sec. 2.5 shows acceleration adds lower-order terms, Eq.(15); 2301.01698 eq.(1.8) for stationary worldlines)
P4 all Hadamard states; the right-hand side is state-independent
P5 g real, smooth, compactly supported; extends to g in W^{2,2}(R); fails for discontinuous g (sharp switching)

P6 Eq.(4): <T00> < rho (rho a constant) throughout an interval of duration tau at the point; sampler g in C0^oo of the open interval; the infimum is the least eigenvalue of d^4/dt^4 with clamped ends (footnote 7: Sobolev analysis, Fewster-Teo [36]); C printed only as 'C ~ 3.17'
P7 'The bound is known not to be optimal' (said of Eq.(3); Eq.(4) inherits it)

P8 Casimir a priori bound: plates at z = +-L/2 in otherwise flat spacetime; inertial trajectory parallel to the plates; l = distance to nearest plate; locality/causality argument that for durations < 2l the Minkowski QEI applies (based on Fewster-Pfenning [31], see also [20]); energy density supposed constant along the trajectory; applies to all stationary Hadamard states
P9 Casimir comparison: massless minimally coupled scalar (boundary condition not stated in the passage; the printed functional form is the Dirichlet one, re-derived here)
hypothesis_drift: ATTRIBUTION (not an error): Fewster prints only 'C ~ 3.17' and the clamped-eigenvalue characterisation; he does NOT print C = mu_1^4/(16 pi^2) or cos(mu_1)cosh(mu_1) = 1. The tree attributes the closed form to 'Fewster 1208.5399 Eq. (4)' at noise.py:80-83, specthm.py:921-925, bounds.py:270-273 and the canonical entry names. The closed form is the tree's own (correct) computation -- re-derived here (boundary determinant = 2k^2(1 - cos k cosh k), mu_1 = 4.730040744862704026, C = 3.169857938310468). achievable.py:232-240 states it correctly ('Computed here by bisection ... reproducing Fewster's printed C ~ 3.17').

DROPPED in one use: bounds.py:60-66 and casimir_fraction_of_bound (bounds.py:340-366) use the 3-7% to conclude 'CASIMIR DOES NOT SATURATE IT' and to code FORD_ROMAN_K_IS_WRONG = True (bounds.py:324; ledger W2). The a priori bound is built from Eq.(3), which Fewster states 'is known not to be optimal' (p.10), and from a window 2l fixed by a causality argument rather than by optimisation. The 3-7% therefore shows Casimir sits at 3-7% of THIS valid bound; it does not show how far Casimir sits from the SHARP bound, which is at least as tight and possibly much tighter. bounds.py carries no optimality caveat at that site (grep 'optimal' in bounds.py: no hit); the caveat is carried only at achievable.py:256 for the corridor use.

RELABEL: bounds.py:55-66 frames the withdrawn claim as 'Casimir is the Ford-Roman bound saturated' and withdraws it with Fewster's a priori bound. Fewster's Eq.(4) constant comes from the Fewster-Eveson (1/16pi^2) INT g''^2 form with the optimal clamped sampler, not from Ford-Roman's Lorentzian -3/(32 pi^2 t0^4); the canonical names also write 'Ford-Roman / Fewster flat-space bound'. The withdrawal is licensed for Fewster's bound; for Ford-Roman's own bound bounds.py:67-70 cites gr-qc/9510071 separately (a different key, not audited here).

DISCREPANCY CARRIED: Fewster's text layer prints the Casimir constant as pi^2/(1140 L^4); the standard value for the Dirichlet massless scalar is pi^2/(1440 L^4) (re-derived here two ways: zeta mode sum E/A = -pi^2/(1440 L^3), and the periodic a = 2L image family -pi^2/(90 a^4)). The tree copies 1140 at bounds.py:347 and bounds.py:350. It moves the midpoint fraction 6.7597% -> 6.7028% and leaves '3-7%' intact. The selftest pin near(mid, 0.0682, rel 1e-2) at bounds.py:557 passes on 1140 (|rel| 0.0088) and WOULD FAIL on 1440 (|rel| 0.0172): the pin is keyed to the misprint. A misprint, recorded, not a refutation.

NAMED, NOT DROPPED: application of the Minkowski/inertial bound on the curved corridor -- specthm H_flat 'ASSUMED' (specthm.py:900-985), noise.py H2 'FAILS ON THE CORRIDOR, b/l_G = 61.237', achievable.py:257,370 'boundary-free flat space'. EXTENSION, NAMED: ledger.py:406-411 'STATE-INDEPENDENT over Hadamard states, so no branch of any decomposition escapes it' -- the source's state-independence is over Hadamard states of THIS free minimally coupled field; the ledger names the escape ('a matter model outside its hypotheses -- see O1'), and bounds.py:283-285 cites Sec. 5.1 (nonminimal coupling sustains arbitrarily negative densities over arbitrarily large volumes, READ p.44).

SCOPE OF 'OPTIMAL': fewsterteo.py:41-42 'C_F ... at the OPTIMAL COMPACTLY SUPPORTED sampler' -- correct for the Eq.(3) functional (Galerkin check here converges down onto mu_1^4 from 504); it is optimal for a bound that is itself 'known not to be optimal', so -C/tau^4 is the best this inequality gives, not the sharp QEI floor. For the corridor this is conservative (a sharper QEI can only refuse harder); for the Casimir ratio it runs the other way (the true ratio to the sharp bound is >= 3-7%).

(B) Fewster-Teo c_2 = 16 pi^2. (C) image-sum <phi^2>, improvement-term sign (trace vanishes iff xi = 1/6), minimal-coupling term matches Fewster's second term exactly; conformal constant is 1440 by two routes, so the printed 1140 is a DISCREPANCY (misprint), recorded. (D) the ratio is monotone in |z|, from 16/mu_1^4 = 3.1964% at the plates to 6.7597% (1140) / 6.7028% (1440) at the midpoint; Fewster's '3-7%' holds either way; the tree's 0.067597 and 0.031976 reproduce with 1140; bounds.py's pin 0.0682 passes only on 1140. lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for this result. What the author had: Eq.(3)/(4) is a theorem of free QFT in Minkowski space with no measured input; C is a pure number fixed by an eigenvalue problem, and the Casimir comparison uses a theoretical density. There is no datum that a later measurement could move: re-derived here, C = 3.16985793831 agrees with the printed 'C ~ 3.17', and the physical constants the tree adds downstream (hbar, c exact; G unchanged CODATA 2018 -> 2022) do not move 71.256. Evidence the other way, also found: (i) a genuine error in print -- the Casimir constant 1140 should be 1440 -- which is a misprint that moves the midpoint ratio by 0.057 percentage points and not the '3-7%' conclusion, but which the tree copied and against which its own selftest pin 0.0682 is tuned; (ii) incompleteness Fewster himself states: 'The bound is known not to be optimal', and 'There remains an interesting question as to why the Casimir energy density is a comparatively small proportion of the allowed bound' -- i.e. the gap between the Casimir density and the bound is an open question in the source, not a measured distance to the true QEI floor. What would change the conclusion is not new data but a sharper QEI in the plate geometry (e.g., a boundary-aware QEI along the trajectory); that is a mathematical gap, not a data gap. Verdict on M's hypothesis for THIS result: not supported as 'lacked data'; supported in the narrower form 'incomplete', exactly where the author says so.
grade_evidence: Eq.(3)/(4) as used for the corridor STANDS on its own: the published statement and hypotheses match the tree's use (the non-Minkowski application is carried as the named hypothesis H_flat, not dropped), and the constant re-derives exactly (rederive A1-A10, 0 FAIL). The grade is NARROWED because of the Sec. 1.3 Casimir use: bounds.py:60-66 / 340-366 / 557-562 turn '3-7% of Fewster's a priori bound' into 'CASIMIR DOES NOT SATURATE [Ford-Roman]' (FORD_ROMAN_K_IS_WRONG, ledger W2) without the hypothesis Fewster states on p.10, 'The bound is known not to be optimal'. Holding at 3-7% of a valid non-optimal bound establishes non-saturation of THAT bound only; the distance to the sharp QEI floor is unmeasured and at most 93-97% of it. The relabelling (Fewster's clamped-sampler bound written as 'Ford-Roman') narrows it again. Two discrepancies are recorded, and neither is a refutation: the printed Casimir constant 1140 (correct: 1440, derived two ways) is copied at bounds.py:347,350 and leaves '3-7%' intact, but bounds.py:557's pin 0.0682 at rel 1e-2 passes only on the misprint; and the closed form mu_1^4/(16pi^2) with cos mu cosh mu = 1 is attributed to Fewster's Eq.(4), which prints only 'C ~ 3.17' (the value is right). No computation here contradicts Fewster: WRONG is not available. No datum has moved: DATA-DEPENDENT is not available.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: bounds.py's Casimir withdrawal carries 'relative to Fewster's a priori bound, which is known not to be optimal' (or the claim is restated as 'Casimir is 3.2-6.8% of a valid a priori QEI bound'), and the Ford-Roman label is kept apart from Fewster's bound. The 1140/1440 misprint would still be recorded as a discrepancy either way. To WRONG for the withdrawal (not for Eq.(4)): a sharp QEI in the Dirichlet-plate geometry, READ at source, that the Casimir density saturates, e.g. a boundary-aware worldline bound equal to the Casimir density along some trajectory. To OPEN: none -- every link used here was read or computed. Reading Fewster-Pfenning math-ph/0602042 would upgrade the causality-window argument from READ-VIA-FEWSTER to READ, and could not change Eq.(4).
